children: Brent crude oil inched up to over $106 per barrel on Thursday, testing one-month highs as markets continued to focus on mounting risks to supply in the Middle East. Repeated strikes on commercial vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz resulted in the sinking of a Singapore-flagged container ship, extending the record-high rates for tankers in the Persian Gulf.
The events also dimmed prospects that oil exports from GCC countries could pick up, adding further strain to the global supply backdrop.
On top of that, Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure added to export disruptions, with some tankers reportedly avoiding their usual loading areas.
Consequently, data from the EIA showed that crude oil stockpiles in the US fell by 8.6 million barrels in the week to October 9th, the sharpest decline since February.
In addition, the federal Strategic Petroleum Reserve remained unchanged near its record low.

title: Brent Tests Highest Level in 1 Month
